title: Move cloud/sandbox to ticfac/image and expose it through the compatibility executor
description:
SPEC 12 Phase 4 items 4 and 5. Move cloud/sandbox/** to ticfac/image/** and expose the current SandboxBinding behaviour through a compatibility executor - the thing that lets ticfac's reconciler dispatch a tick to a container at all. cloud/worker/** stays in ticks, and the ticks.sh board must be absent from the Factory deployment (verify, do not assume).

This is where 'cloudflare-sandbox' stops being a name ticfac refuses (substrate_test.go asserts the refusal today, with the phrase 'provenance that lies') and becomes an executor it can dispatch to: start, inspect, cancel, collect, the same four operations the local executors implement.

Note the ownership decision already taken in 5bp: ticks owns cloud/sandbox and ticfac vendors it at a pinned ref, verified byte-for-byte in CI. This move has to settle whether that survives, is reversed, or the pin moves - do not leave two copies drifting again.
notes:
2026-09-18 17:44 - READ l9n's note before starting. This tick carries the same SPEC notation - 'move cloud/sandbox/** to ticfac/image/**' - and ticfac/ names the REPOSITORY, not a directory inside it. The destination is image/ at the root. l9n took it literally and created a nested ticfac/cloudflare/, which cost eleven path corrections to unpick.

Expect the same class of breakage here: anything that encodes how deep cloud/sandbox sits. Known already, because l9n hit them from the other side - wrangler.toml's [[containers]] image path and bundle.go's sandboxRelativeToBundle both point AT cloud/sandbox and both had to move when the factory moved. Moving the sandbox itself will move them again.

Grep for the pattern rather than fixing one failure at a time: paths with repeated ../, //go:embed patterns, and any constant naming the old location.
2026-09-18 18:21 - From l9n's finding 4c8a55f8 (Phase 4 run epic-ncv).

cloud/sandbox/README.md, common.sh and worker.sh still reference cloud/factory/src/... for the control-plane files they describe. Those trees are DIGEST-PINNED to ticks here (internal/sandboxpin), so l9n could not edit them — editing a vendored tree in place is how a pin stops meaning anything.

So this tick owns the doc alignment: when you move the image context and re-sync the pin, the same bump carries the path fixes. Do NOT hand-edit the vendored copy; fix it in ticks and re-sync.

Triaged into this tick rather than filed separately — a second tick would race this one for the same pin bump.
2026-09-19 09:25 - 2026-09-19 — the xo2 blocker is REMOVED and the edge reversed: xo2 is now blocked by k4s.

The old edge was a cycle. xo2 says in its own description that the sequence is 'ncv ports the behaviour into a ticfac cloud executor, ncv's gate proves it, and only then does a retirement tick delete the tk side'. So xo2 waits on ncv. But k4s is a CHILD of ncv and was blocked by xo2 — k4s -> xo2 -> ncv -> k4s. Nothing could move, and Phase 4 could not complete.

k4s never needed anything xo2 produces. k4s IS part of the porting xo2 is waiting for: it exposes SandboxBinding through a compatibility executor. What it needs is for tk's cloud drivers to still EXIST as the reference to port from, and that is exactly what xo2 guarantees by forbidding their deletion.

So the dependency ran backwards. k4s comes first; xo2 becomes the retirement tick it describes itself as, after ncv proves the executor works.

acceptance_criteria: ticfac dispatches a tick to a Cloudflare sandbox through an executor implementing the same four operations as the local ones, and the attempt's records are indistinguishable in shape from a local attempt's. cloud/worker stays in ticks and the ticks.sh board is verified absent from the deployment. The 5bp ownership decision is restated or replaced explicitly.
